name: hammer

attributes.attribute: Celtic symbol of divine force tied to the god with the hammer
associated with Taranis, Dis Pater, Silvanus, and Sucellus
interpreted as storm and thunder, earth fertility, or winter blight
carried a club or mallet that may be the Irish form of the hammer

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The hammer is a Celtic symbol of divine power. The "god with the hammer" was a common image among the continental Celts. People called him Taranis, Dis Pater, Silvanus, and Sucellus. He appeared strong, mature, and bearded. The hammer stood for the force and energy of such gods. Some readers tie him to storm and thunder, though the texts give no firm sign of that meaning. Others connect him to the earth's fertility. He often carries a cup, a common symbol of earthly energy, which supports that view. A minority sees the hammer as the blighting force of winter. The club or mallet of the Dagda may be the Irish form of this divine hammer.
objective: Document the hammer as the symbol of the continental Celtic god with the hammer.
key_results: Record the hammer's divine names and appearance.
List the interpretations of storm, fertility, and winter.
Note the Dagda's club as a possible Irish form.
evidence: Monaghan, P. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (2008): hammer entry.
